name: Uranus
fact: Uranus rotates on its side — axial tilt 98°. Its north pole points almost directly at the Sun for half its 84-year orbit.
bio: Tipped almost on its side (97.77°). Each pole gets 42 years of continuous sunlight, then 42 years of darkness. Almost certainly caused by an ancient massive collision.

links.l: Uranus Orbiter and Probe — Decadal Survey

science_sections.why: Uranus's 97.8° tilt means it rotates on its side — each pole gets ~42 years of continuous sunlight, then ~42 years of darkness.
The inclination of the planet matters less than the tilt of its rotation axis — Uranus has the most dramatic axial inclination in the system, even though its orbital inclination is modest (0.77°).
The five major Uranian moons (Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, Oberon) share Uranus's tilt — they orbit in the equatorial plane, which is nearly perpendicular to the ecliptic.
No spacecraft has visited Uranus since Voyager 2 (1986). A Uranus orbiter is a top NASA Decadal-Survey priority for the 2030s.
